_README: Global Search RANKING (6726) + fuzzy remainder (6725) on sv9160. Everything ZZAUTOTEST-adjacent and disposable. Generated by build_ranking_manifest.py - never hand-edited.
_THE_DESIGN_RULE: One distinctive keyword per case, carried by that case's 2-3 records only, which differ in EXACTLY ONE signal. Verified private: every keyword returned NOTHING on sv9160 on 2026-09-17 before these records were created.
_DEPENDENT_PASS: Work orders, purchase orders, vendor invoices and stock levels are layered on afterwards by the chain scripts; the records here are their anchors.

records._why: PREFIX: the name STARTS with the keyword. Must rank first.
WHOLE WORD mid-name. Must rank below the prefix match and above the typo.

FUZZY: one edit from the keyword (X->Y), reachable only by fuzzy matching. Must rank LAST. 🔴 It was ZZPREFIXX, which is the keyword PLUS a letter - so it STARTS with the keyword, prefix-matched, and ranked FIRST, inverting the very order the case asserts. A typo record must be one edit away AND not a prefix of, or prefixed by, the keyword.
Gets an OPEN work order attached in the dependent pass. Must rank above its twin.
Deliberately NO work order and never opened. The control.
Owner for the ZZASSETLIFT assets. Deliberately carries NO keyword, so searching ZZASSETLIFT returns the two assets and nothing else.

records.type: Contact (a PERSON at a customer company)
records._why: The Customer entity the asset create requires. Its name carries no keyword, so it cannot pollute the ZZASSETLIFT assets group.
Older model year ON AN OPEN WORK ORDER. Must still outrank the newer idle one - which is the whole point: the open-work-order lift beats the model-year tiebreak.
NEWER model year, no work order, never opened. If this ranks first the lift is not applied.
Gets OPEN purchase orders in the dependent pass. Must rank above its twin.
Deliberately NO purchase orders. The control.
Created first and NOT touched again. Otherwise identical to its twin.
Identical match quality, but UPDATED LAST by the seeder, so it must win the tie.
Stocked to a positive quantity in the dependent pass. Must rank above the out-of-stock twin.

payload.name: ZZSTOCKPART Brake Drum Out Of Stock

records._why: Left at zero on hand. 🔴 It must still APPEAR - the case asserts out-of-stock is ranked lower, NOT hidden. A missing row here is a different (and reportable) behaviour from a low row.
Sold/used and viewed in the dependent pass. Must rank above the quiet twin.
Same stock state, no activity. Isolates recent-activity from in-stock-vs-out.
The COMPANY NAME deliberately contains neither ZZCONTACTONLY nor the contact phone. The only route to this record is its contact - which is exactly what the case measures.

records.type: Contact (a PERSON at a customer company)
records._why: Carries the ZZCONTACTONLY token and a distinctive phone. Searching either must return the COMPANY, flagged as a contact match.
SHORT token "Ab" - two letters. Querying "Ac" (one edit) must NOT drag it in.
LONG token "Abcde" - five letters. Querying "Abcdf" (one edit) SHOULD find it. The contrast between these two rows is the whole case.
POSITIVE quantity. Must rank above the zero-quantity twin.
ZERO on hand. 🔴 It must still be RETURNED - the case asserts out-of-stock ranks lower, not that it disappears. A missing row here is a different and reportable behaviour.
Same stock state as its twin, so stock cannot explain any ordering difference. The activity signal is applied in the dependent pass.
Identical stock, no activity. The control that isolates recent-activity from in-stock.

records.type: Contact (a PERSON at a customer company)
records._why: A work order needs a contact as its customer_id. Named without the keyword so it cannot add a row to the customers group the case counts.

The open work order needs an asset. Deliberately NOT a ZZASSETLIFT vehicle - giving one of those an open work order would break C55709, whose whole point is that only ONE of its two assets has one. 🔴 And its unit/VIN carry NO keyword either: named CUSTOPEN-01 at first, it matched ZZCUSTOPEN and added an asset row to a customers-ranking case.

find._why: ?search= is broken on /api/work-orders, so these are verified by the ids the seeder captured at create time.

records._why: THE SIGNAL for C55708: an OPEN work order on ZZCUSTOPEN Haulage Open and none on its twin. Left in its created (estimate) state, which is open.
THE SIGNAL for C55709: the 2019 asset is on an open work order, the 2025 is not. The case asserts that lift beats the newer model year.
FIVE open work orders. Must rank above its twin.
ONE open work order. Not zero - the case is "more beats fewer", not "some beats none", which C55708 already covers.

records._why: Same, for the quiet twin.

Carries the five open work orders. 🔴 Its unit and VIN carry NO keyword - an asset is indexed under its OWNER'S name, so it will answer ZZOPENCOUNT anyway; giving it the keyword too would add nothing and risk confusing the assets group.
Carries the single open work order.
FIVE open work orders - the signal under test. Left in their created (estimate) state, which is open.
ONE open work order.
Matched on its NAME. Must rank above the address-only match.
Matched ONLY on a secondary field: the keyword is in its ADDRESS and nowhere in its name. If this outranks the name match the primary-name bonus is not being applied.

Accents on the e and the i. BOTH the plain and the accented spelling must find this one row - so there must be exactly ONE record carrying the token, or "both find the same customer" cannot be read off the result.
APOSTROPHE. Must be found by ZZPUNC OBrien and by the punctuated form.
HYPHEN. Must be found by ZZPUNC Smith Jones and by the punctuated form. Two records, one keyword, because the case asks for both punctuation kinds.
The part whose DESCRIPTION carries the word. A sound-alike of "Alternator" must NOT return it.

THE STOCK ROW. Without it the catalogue part is invisible to search - so the case would have read as "the part is correctly not returned" when the part was never findable at all, which is a pass for entirely the wrong reason.
THE CONTROL, and the case cannot be read without it: a NAME must still sound-alike match. If neither row comes back the sound-alike was simply wrong, not proof of names-only behaviour.

Its NAME BEGINS with a real work-order number, so typing that number produces the strongest possible competing name match - and the case asserts the pinned exact-ID row still wins.
